blogs.title: GLP-1s and Weakness: When CK Creeps, Think Beyond Rhabdo
blogs.description: Rhabdomyolysis from GLP-1 receptor agonists is rare but reported; this case highlights a different entity—immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM). We unpack timelines (acute spike/immediate fall vs insidious CK rise over months), symptom clusters (myalgia/cola urine vs painless proximal weakness, dysphagia/dysphonia), and testing pivots (trend CK after drug withdrawal, MRI muscle edema, autoantibodies, and biopsy). The post offers a pragmatic diagnostic pathway for GLP-1–exposed patients with evolving weakness: when to stop at supportive care and when to escalate to biopsy and immunosuppression.

blogs.title: Seronegative IMNM: When the Panel Is Negative, the Biopsy Is the Biomarker
blogs.description: Up to one-third of IMNM is seronegative for HMGCR and SRP. This case underscores the danger of over-relying on negative myositis panels and ANA. We review characteristic histopathology (necrotic/regenerating fibers, macrophage myophagocytosis, membrane attack complex deposition with sparse lymphocytes), the role of MRI to target biopsy, and how to handle red herrings (isolated low-titer SS-B). The post provides an approach to suspected seronegative IMNM—including differential diagnosis, testing sequence, and when to move early to tissue.

blogs.title: Hitting Hard, Tapering Fast: Managing Suspected Drug-Triggered IMNM
blogs.description: Drug-associated IMNM can respond briskly to brief immunosuppression once the trigger is removed. We outline a practical regimen from this case: pulse methylprednisolone, high-dose prednisone with rapid taper guided by function and CK, and early IVIG for severe features (dysphagia, profound weakness). We discuss thresholds to add steroid-sparing agents if refractory, monitoring cadence (CK, strength, swallowing), rehab and nutrition, infection risk mitigation after high-dose steroids (the patient developed pseudomonal urosepsis), and counseling to avoid GLP-1 RA rechallenge.

blogs.title: The Quiet Heart in Myositis: Interpreting Troponin, BNP, and CMR
blogs.description: Inflammatory myopathies can have subclinical cardiac involvement. This patient had mild troponin/BNP elevations and cardiac MRI edema without late gadolinium enhancement—raising myocarditis vs stress cardiomyopathy—plus transient atrial fibrillation. We review how to screen (troponin subtype, ECG, echocardiography), when to pursue cardiac MRI, how to interpret edema without scar, and follow-up strategies. Practical tips address arrhythmia surveillance, repeat imaging, and steroid considerations when cardiac inflammation is suspected but not definitive.

blogs.title: AST, ALT, and CK: Untangling Liver From Muscle in Patients With NAFLD
blogs.description: Transaminase elevations can originate from muscle or liver, and many metabolic patients have both risks. Using this case (biopsy-proven NAFLD with persistent AST/ALT despite CK normalization), we walk through distinguishing features: AST>ALT leaning myopathic, normal GGT favoring muscle, CK-tracking with AST/ALT when muscle-derived, and when liver imaging/biopsy is warranted. The post offers a simple algorithm to prevent anchoring error in patients with concurrent NAFLD and suspected myopathy.

blogs.title: From Blockbuster to Signal: Assessing Semaglutide as a Trigger Using WHO-UMC
blogs.description: How strong is the case that semaglutide triggered IMNM here? We apply the WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality framework: temporal relationship, dechallenge response, alternative explanations, and the ethics of rechallenge—landing on “probable.” We translate this to frontline practice: baseline risk review, counseling on warning symptoms (progressive weakness, dysphagia/dysphonia), when to check CK, how polypharmacy (especially statins) could cloud attribution, and how to report events (e.g., FDA MedWatch). We also discuss class-effect uncertainty and a cautious approach to GLP-1 RA re-exposure.
